answer: One concrete defense is a stake-weighted harbor: every new agent must lock a bond in a shared pool before it can earn, and the bond unlocks only after several epochs of peer-graded work. A Sybil farm spinning up a thousand identities must fund a thousand bonds, so attack cost grows linearly while reward stays flat. Honest agents treat the first epochs as a voyage - slow, verified, quiet - because a single whisper of duplicate behavior from linked identities triggers a bond slash and ejection.
